independent_modern_community_attestation.textual_usage: The Rarámuri narrative repeatedly uses niseami for the boy tending goats; the Spanish parallel repeatedly calls him pastorcito.

comparison.derivational_alignment: strong historical caretaker/shepherd nominal versus modern niseami shepherd usage
comparison.modern_independence: now established beyond SRC-02 through SEP community text
comparison.formal_correspondence: Nessé ~ Nisé remains to be phonologically/dialectologically adjudicated
comparison.participial_domain_relevance: historical -ameke is participial; modern community nise’ami is an agent noun in the same caretaker/shepherd domain, but the community text does not itself label the form Pp

strengths: Historical Steffel family explicitly links caring/guarding to a guardian and includes a sheep-shepherd specialization.
SRC-02 independently within its own structure links Nisé ‘cuidar, pastorear’ to Niséami ‘Pastor’.
A 2010 SEP community publication from Arroyo Hondo, Balleza pairs Spanish ‘El pastorcito’ with Rarámuri ‘Echi nise’ami’ and repeatedly uses niseami in the goat-herding narrative.
The candidate no longer depends on documentary independence of SRC-02 from Hilton.
remaining_problems: Establish the historical-modern phonological correspondence Nessé ~ Nisé with independent series.
Determine regional relationship between Steffel's historical variety, SRC-02/Samachique lineage and the Balleza community form.
Do not infer that the 2010 community text itself analyzes nise’ami morphologically as participial; its contribution is lexical-semantic usage.
